caption:
Global Metadata
Basic Attributes: bpm is 92. key is G major, and scale is major. Modern Acoustic Pop / Indie-Pop Duet with cinematic build.
Global Emotional Progression: The track opens nostalgic and intimate, a female voice almost spoken over gentle fingerstyle acoustic guitar and soft piano as she finds a box of old polaroids, with a faint room-noise texture and a distant laugh. The first verse is warm storytelling from the female lead, a shy first meeting, then the male lead answers with his own memory in a soft sincere voice over the same gentle bed. The pre-chorus, sung together, gathers tension and hope, and opens into a big, singable chorus in close male and female harmony with strummed guitar, full piano, warm bass, light drums and swelling strings. The second pair of verses is the fight: the male lead first, the arrangement thinning to piano and a held bass note, tense and quiet, then the female lead brings the reconciliation and the warmth returns. A shortened second chorus lands softer and closer. The instrumental break is a soft piano and acoustic guitar duet with a light string swell and ambient room sounds, distant traffic, a laugh, a door closing, before the band returns. The bridge is raw and honest, half-time, stripped to guitar and voice, the female lead then the male lead trading lines about the night he almost left, then both voices building together as they choose each other. The final chorus lifts a whole step brighter, triumphant and grateful, both voices together at full strength with the anthemic post-chorus chant of polaroids and phone screens, and the outro returns to the quiet intro texture, female then male then both in gentle harmony on we're still here.
Application Scenarios & Imagery: A couple on the bedroom floor with a shoebox of old polaroids, a rainy café window and shared earphones, a night train with her asleep on his shoulder, a kitchen at three in the morning, a blurry puffy-eyed selfie the morning after a fight, a packed bag on the bed, a handwritten list taped to a living room wall, two people dancing in a kitchen, the tender ending of a couple's story that is still being written.
Sonics & Production Profile: Wide, cinematic soundstage with deep stereo pads and a tightly centered vocal. Modern pop-R&B polish: controlled low end with weighty sub-bass and 808s, scooped low-mids for vocal clarity, crisp airy top end. Dynamics are contained in the verses and open dramatically in the choruses. Generous plate and hall reverb on atmospheric elements, with the lead vocal kept close and dry for intimacy.

Vocal Details
Vocal Gender & Timbre: Singer A (Female). A young-adult lead with a warm, slightly husky tone; intimate and breathy in the low register, gaining a raw, expressive rasp as she pushes into her upper chest voice.
Duet Partner: Singer B (Male). A soft, sincere baritone-tenor, unforced and conversational, warm in the low register and gentle at the top, harmonising just beneath the female lead rather than competing with her.
Duet Structure: The intro is the female lead alone. The first verse is the female lead, the second verse is the male lead, the pre-chorus and chorus are both voices in harmony. After the first chorus the male lead sings the fight verse and the female lead sings the reconciliation verse. The bridge alternates female then male then both together. The final chorus, post-chorus and outro are both voices together.
Vocal Style: Confessional and conversational in the verses, sitting close to the microphone with audible breath and soft consonants. The pre-chorus builds urgency through rising phrasing and tighter rhythmic delivery. The chorus is belted, powerful and slightly raspy at the peaks, with emotional cracks left intact rather than smoothed over. The bridge returns to near-spoken fragility before the final build.
Harmony/Backing Vocals: Stacked female harmonies thicken the chorus. Layered male and female harmonies join on the final hook for maximum width and lift. Airy wordless vocal echoes drift through the outro.
Vocal FX: Close, dry lead with subtle plate reverb and a short slapback delay. Throw delays on chorus phrase endings. The outro vocals are treated with long, washed-out reverb tails and rhythmic echo.

Arrangement
Instrument Lifecycle Description (Primary/Secondary Layering):
Primary: Acoustic guitar is the spine of the song, fingerstyle in the intro, verses and bridge, opening into warm strumming in the choruses, present from the first bar to the last. Piano sits beside it throughout, sparse single notes under the verses and full chords in the choruses. Warm bass, a sub layer with a light electric bass on top, enters at the first pre-chorus.
Secondary: Soft synth pads and cinematic strings enter in the choruses and swell through the instrumental break and under the bridge build. Finger snaps, shaker, a soft kick and snare carry the groove from the first chorus. Subtle ambient textures act as ear candy: room noise, a distant laugh, a phone notification chime on the good morning text line, a door closing in the instrumental break.
Groove & Foundation Progression: The intro and first verses are free and gentle over guitar and piano with no drums. Finger snaps and shaker enter in the pre-chorus, and a soft kick and snare land with the first chorus in a warm mid-tempo pop groove. The fight verse drops to piano and a held bass note with almost no percussion. The bridge is half-time, guitar and voice, then builds with strings and snaps. The final chorus lifts to a brighter key with the fullest drums of the track and both voices together, and the outro returns to the intro texture and fades on guitar and piano.
Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX: The intro and outro carry warm room noise and the faint sound of polaroids being shuffled. A phone notification chime sounds once under the good morning text line. The instrumental break features a soft piano and acoustic guitar duet with a light string swell and ambient room sounds, distant traffic, a laugh, a door closing. String swells and reverse cymbals mark the transitions into each chorus.
lyrics:
[intro]
I found a box beneath our bed,
Full of polaroids we never framed.
Your handwriting on every back,
Little dates and silly names.

[verse]
First photo, you in that old grey hoodie,
Coffee in your hand, trying not to stare.
I was pretending I didn't notice,
But I noticed everything about you there.
Rain on the window, cheap earphones sharing,
Your playlist full of songs I didn't know.
You said, this one feels like how you laugh,
And I fell a little, slow and low.

[verse]
Next one, you asleep on my shoulder,
On that night train to nowhere special.
I didn't sleep, I just watched you breathe,
Thinking, please let this be real, not accidental.
We were scared of saying I love you,
So we said it in the way we stayed.
In the way you saved my side of the sofa,
In the way I learned your favourite shade.

[pre-chorus]
We didn't know we were building a forever,
We were just trying to get through today.
But every little good morning text
Was a brick in the house where our hearts could stay.

[chorus]
We're still writing our story
In polaroids and phone screens,
In late-night talks and are you okay,
In I'm here and please don't go away.
We're still writing our story
Through the mess and the in-betweens,
Every fight, every I was wrong,
Every stay when we could've gone.
If love is a film, then we're the slow scene,
Not the highlight, just the parts in between.
We're still writing our story,
In polaroids and phone screens.

[verse]
Remember that kitchen at 3 a.m.,
When we fought about nothing and everything?
You said, maybe we're just not enough,
I said nothing, let the silence sing.
You cried in the bathroom, I sat on the floor,
Holding a mug I didn't drink.
I was scared that if I knocked too loud,
You'd say, this is it, this is the end.

[verse]
But then you came out with your eyes all red,
Said, I don't wanna win, I just want us.
I dropped every argument I had,
And held you through the shaking and the dust.
That photo's blurry, taken next day,
Both of us laughing, puffy-eyed.
Caption on the back just says,
We almost broke. We didn't die.

[chorus]
We're still writing our story
In polaroids and phone screens,
Every fight, every I was wrong,
Every stay when we could've gone.

[instrumental]

[bridge]
There's one I haven't shown you yet,
Taken the night you almost left.
You packed a bag, then sat back down,
Said, I don't know if I can do this again.
I said, I love you, but I'm tired
Of the distance, of the almosts, of the maybes.
You said, then let's stop being almost,
And start being honest, even if it's scary.
So we wrote a list on the living room wall,
What we're scared of, what we need, what we'll change.
And that choice, again and again,
Is the reason we're still here today.

[chorus]
We're still writing our story
In polaroids and phone screens,
In I'm proud of you and I messed up,
In let's talk and give me space, please.
We're still writing our story
Through the mess and the in-betweens,
Every scar, every we survived,
Every us when it could've been me.
If love is a film, then we're the long cut,
Not the trailer, just the parts no one sees.
We're still writing our story,
In polaroids and phone screens.

[post-chorus]
Polaroids and phone screens,
Polaroids and phone screens.
We're still here, we're still here,
In polaroids and phone screens.

[outro]
I put the box back under the bed,
But I kept a few in my pocket today.
Just in case we forget who we are,
When the world gets loud and the colours fade.
We're still here.
We're still here.
